subject: Ledger routing & tax-tagging for split payments
messages:
From: BrightBridge Finance <ap@brightbridge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: split billing across BrightBridge legal entities + tax tagging

Hi Marcus / Laura,

Thanks for the quick chat this morning. As discussed, BrightBridge needs Redwood to support multi-entity billing for our account. We have three procurement entities that each pay for different product categories and cost centers. To make AP and audit happy we need either: a) separate invoices per entity for the same billing period, or b) a consolidated invoice with invoice lines pre-tagged with entity codes so our ERP can auto-allocate.

Attached is a matrix (BRB_payment_matrix.xlsx) showing monthly consumption by cost center, the preferred legal entity for that charge, and the tax jurisdiction for each line. A few important constraints from our side:

- EU entity (BrightBridge EU GmbH) requires VAT-exempt handling for some transactions and specific tax id stamping on invoice header.
- AP needs GL account suggestions per cost center to map to our chart of accounts.
- For services billed in USD but paid by entity in local currency, we need the invoice to show the USD amount and an optional allocation column for their ERP to accept multi-currency payments.

Could you confirm whether Redwood can:
1) Issue separate invoices per legal entity for the same billing period (preferred), including entity-specific tax headers.
2) Alternatively, provide a consolidated invoice CSV export with per-line entity_code and GL_code fields so we can ingest into our ledger.

We can provide sample PO numbers per entity once you confirm the approach. Also attached: BRB_tax_exempt_cert.pdf for your tax team.

Thanks,

Lola Mendes
AP Manager, BrightBridge Inc.
ap@brightbridge.com
(555) 402-7781

Attachment: BRB_payment_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet)
Attachment: BRB_tax_exempt_cert.pdf (pdf)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: BrightBridge Finance <ap@brightbridge.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: split billing across BrightBridge legal entities + tax tagging

Hi Lola — thanks for the clear matrix and the tax cert. This is doable but we want to pick the option that minimizes manual reconciliation for both sides. High-level options and tradeoffs: 

Option A — Separate invoices per legal entity (recommended if AP wants clean vendor invoices):
- Creation: We run separate invoice runs for each legal entity and include entity-specific tax headers and registration numbers.
- Payment: Each invoice will have its own payment remittance information (bank account/ACH instructions or payment link).
- Pros: Straightforward for BrightBridge AP; better for audit.
- Cons: More invoice objects to manage on our side; potential small variance in rounding for multi-currency.

Option B — Consolidated invoice with per-line allocation (CSV-friendly):
- Creation: Single PDF invoice for the account + accompanying CSV export where each line includes entity_code, GL_code, tax_jurisdiction, and net/gross amounts.
- Payment: One payment can be applied externally across entities using your ERP split logic.
- Pros: Single invoice in your vendor record; less operational overhead for Redwood.
- Cons: Your AP must support automated split application; more work on your ERP side.

From an implementation perspective we can:
- Add two new export fields to our billing API: entity_code and gl_code.
- Tag invoice headers with tax_id when we issue per-entity invoices.
- Support a combined CSV export as part of the billing run.

Next asks from Redwood to finalize:
1) Can you confirm which entity corresponds to each PO in the matrix?
2) Which option (A or B) is preferred for the pilot month (Nov 2026)?
3) Are there any bank or mandate requirements for the EU entity that would affect remittance instructions?

I attached our initial GL mapping file (Redwood_GL_map_v1.csv) showing suggested GL_code values; finance will refine. If you prefer a pilot, we can do Nov as a single pilot cycle and iterate.

Thanks — I’ll loop in Finance to confirm tax stamping details.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachment: Redwood_GL_map_v1.csv (csv)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Ledger routing & tax-tagging for split payments

Marcus / Karthik — finance here. Quick notes after reviewing the BRB matrix and the GL map: 

- We can support Option A (separate invoices per legal entity) with the following guardrails:
  * Each invoice will include entity_name and tax_id in the header and a tax_jurisdiction field per line.
  * We will append an allocation column (entity_code) to the invoice PDF and the machine-export CSV for reconciliation.
  * For multi-currency lines, we will include both the invoice currency amount and the USD canonical amount used for our internal reports.

- VAT / Tax handling:
  * For the EU entity: If BrightBridge provides the valid VAT exemption certificate (we received BRB_tax_exempt_cert.pdf), we will mark the invoice as VAT-exempt and include the exemption reference in the invoice notes.
  * For withholdings: If any jurisdiction requires withholding tax, we will flag those lines and include a withholding note; however, calculation and remittance responsibility remains with the payer per local law (we can provide gross amounts and a withholdable amount column).

- GL codes: Please confirm whether BrightBridge wants us to write GL_code into the invoice line metadata (CSV) or include it only in the accompanying CSV export. Writing GL_code on the PDF can clutter the human-readable invoice; recommend CSV only and a short human-readable cost-center label on the PDF line.

- Workflow & timeline:
  * We can pilot with a single billing date (Nov 30, 2026) to generate separate entity invoices plus the consolidated CSV.
  * Reconciliation files (CSV) will be available the morning after invoice generation (Dec 1).
  * We will run a one-week exception window (Dec 1–8) to handle mismatches and final post-invoice adjustments.

Action items for sales (Karthik / Marcus): please confirm pilot go-ahead and provide any PO mapping (PO -> entity_code) by Monday 26 Oct EOD so Finance can lock GL mappings.

Thanks,

Laura Bennett
Head of Finance Ops, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com

Hi Lola / Andrew — looping in next steps and timeline so everybody has the doc of record. Per finance guidance we will proceed with Option A: separate invoices per legal entity with a consolidated CSV export. Summary: 

- Pilot billing date: 2026-11-30 (invoices generated and emailed same day).
- Deliverables: separate PDFs per entity + a machine-readable CSV that includes: invoice_id, invoice_date, line_item_id, amount_usd, amount_local, entity_code, gl_code, tax_jurisdiction, tax_amount, exemption_reference (if applicable).
- Tax handling: BrightBridge EU GmbH will be VAT-exempt on the lines specified in BRB_payment_matrix.xlsx once we validate BRB_tax_exempt_cert.pdf. Please confirm the certificate owner and ensure the cert matches the entity registration.
- Remittance: Each entity invoice will include its own remittance instructions. If BrightBridge wants to push a single payment that is internally split, let us know so we can add a remittance_note field to the CSV.
- PO mapping: Please provide final PO -> entity_code mapping by Mon 26 Oct EOD (per Laura's note).

Links and references:
- Pilot artifacts and GL mapping: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRBW_payment_plan
- Deal record: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/BB-47

- BrightBridge: confirm PO to entity mapping; verify VAT cert owner (Lola) / Due: Mon 26 Oct EOD
- Redwood Finance: finalize GL_code list and confirm sample invoice PDF layout (Laura) / Due: Tue 27 Oct EOD
- Redwood Billing Ops: run pilot invoice generation on Nov 30 and share CSV by Dec 1 (Monica) / Due: 2026-12-01

If there are any legal or banking constraints that prevent per-entity invoices, please surface them now so we can adjust. Otherwise we’ll assume pilot is a go and proceed with the implementation work.

Appreciate the partnership — we’ll keep exception handling tight in the first cycle.

— Marcus
